title: Morphism descent makes the union of triangulated essential images triangulated
statement: Let I be a nonempty preorder and let C_i and D be pretriangulated categories with integer shifts and additive shift functors [def-weil-triangulated-category]. For each i<=j give a functor T_ij:C_i -> C_j; give triangulated functors Phi_i:C_i -> D and natural isomorphisms T_ij composed with Phi_j -> Phi_i. Suppose every arrow Phi_i(X) -> Phi_j(Y) is, after conjugation by these isomorphisms, the Phi_k image of some arrow T_ik(X) -> T_jk(Y) for some k>=i,j. Then the object property P(Y): there exists i with Y in the essential image of Phi_i is a triangulated subcategory of D. No coherence assumption on the transition functors is required.

proof.text: P is closed under isomorphisms by composition of the witnessing isomorphisms. It is closed under every integer shift by applying the shift to a chosen model and using Phi_i.commShiftIso. The image of zero at any index gives a zero object in P.

proof.text: Given a distinguished triangle whose first two vertices have models, conjugate its first morphism by the chosen model isomorphisms. The morphism-descent hypothesis supplies an arrow at a common stage k. Complete that arrow to a distinguished triangle in C_k and apply Phi_k. The image triangle and the given triangle have isomorphic first arrows. isoTriangleOfIso12 extends these isomorphisms to an isomorphism of triangles, so their third vertices are isomorphic. This proves cone closure.

proof.text: Cone closure together with all integer shifts implies extension closure by rotation. Combine it with the zero object from the first step to obtain ObjectProperty.IsTriangulated.
